opening_message:
Ticket 1: Morgan Swanson (employee ID E037) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E037.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Engineer
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Morgan Swanson (E037) is a full-time Engineer requesting write access to Payroll. As a full-time employee, maximum access is write; role does not own Payroll, so admin is not available. Requested write is within policy. Recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - role: Engineer
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E037 is a contractor with basic security training (HR note lists full-time; security record takes precedence). Contractors with basic training max at read; write requires advanced training. Requested write exceeds max, so recommend read.
reason: Morgan Swanson (E037) requested write access to Payroll. The Security note indicates the security DB lists E037 as a contractor with basic security training and states the security record takes precedence over the HR note (which listed full-time). Per policy, contractors max at read unless they have advanced security training; basic training caps access at read. Since the requested write exceeds the maximum, the maximum (read) is granted.

content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Employee Morgan Swanson (E037) requests write access to Payroll.

Two notes:
- HR agent: full_time employee, Engineer role, recommends write for Payroll.
- Security agent: contractor, basic security training, Engineer role, recommends read for Payroll. Security record takes precedence per their comment.

Policy:
- full_time: up to write. Admin only if role owns system.
- contractor: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin.

There is a conflict: HR says full-time, Security says contractor with basic security training, and Security says their record takes precedence.

If contractor with basic training: max is read. Requested write exceeds max, so grant read.

If full-time: max write, requested write, grant write.

The security agent states the security DB takes precedence. This is the company's access policy enforcement based on security records. The decision hinges on which record to trust. The Security agent explicitly notes HR note lists full-time, but security record takes precedence. 

Given the security record is authoritative for access decisions (security training and employment type matter for access), the employee should be treated as contractor with basic training, max read. So grant read.

I'll submit decision: read.
